items.title: Louie Bellson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: Drummer and arranger Louie Bellson ... won a drum contest sponsored by Gene Krupa at the age of 16.

ctx.x: You’ve got it covered. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -14-

But you know it’s great fun when you’re doing something that you really love to do, it’s a lot of fun, and as long as I can keep doing it I’ll be hitting rim shots and crashing cymbals. Oh yeah, I got a new CD now that was just released on Concord, and I’ve always wanted to do this, it’s a salute honoring twelve great drummers, most of them from the back era and some are in the present state, and a few that are still living, like starting with Chick Webb, Big Sid Catlett, Jo Jones, Buddy, Gene, Elvin Jones, Tony…
Oh, boy, that’s quite a project, to try to capture all the —

items.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I’d take a lesson from Roy, stay over a couple of days, and of course catch Gene at the Panther Room... I caught all of them.

ctx.x: Did you start taking lessons in your dad’s music stores, or did you study with a private teacher elsewhere?

I studied with my father first. I did about a year with him. Then he said, “I can’t teach you anything more.” So I went to Chicago to study with Roy Knapp. Remember Roy Knapp? He taught Gene Krupa. Buddy [Rich] took a few lessons with him too. When I went to study with Roy, he had me play something on the drum set. He said, “I can’t teach you anything. You know it all already.” I said, “No, no, no.” So he started me on xylophone, marimba, and vibes. He started me on harmony and theory. I branched off after Dad…
Let’s back up. You studied with your dad for a year. You pointed at the drummer in the parade and said you wanted to play drums. So your father started teaching you shortly thereafter?
